title: Sarai Kale Khan RRTS to Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station: Walking Map, Skywalk & Luggage Transit Guide
description: Check out our special guide for interchange from Sarai Kale Khan RRTS to Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station to have a safe and comfortable journey.
body:
If you are getting off a **Namo Bharat train at Sarai Kale Khan** and your next train departs from **Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station (NZM)**, the two stations are now connected by a dedicated pedestrian facility.

But there is an important detail that older route guides may miss.

The connection is **not simply a short roadside walk anymore**. A dedicated **280-metre Foot Over Bridge (FOB)** connects [Sarai Kale Khan Namo Bharat station](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/stations/sarai-kale-khan.html) with Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station. The FOB has **six automatic travelators**, along with escalators and lifts, making the interchange considerably easier for passengers carrying suitcases, children or other luggage.

There is another important 2026 update: **redevelopment work is underway at the Sarai Kale Khan-side second entry of Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station**. Northern Railway has said that passengers should use **Gate 1 and Gate 2 of the Namo Bharat station and the new FOB** to access Hazrat Nizamuddin during this work.

This guide explains the transfer step by step, including the skywalk, travelators, lifts, escalators, railway gates, luggage strategy, estimated walking time and what to do if you need mobility assistance.

> **Quick answer:** From Sarai Kale Khan Namo Bharat station, follow the signs for **Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station**, enter the dedicated FOB, use the travelators where convenient, and continue toward the railway station through the designated entry. During the current second-entry redevelopment, passengers approaching from the Namo Bharat side are directed through **Namo Bharat Gate 1/2 and the new FOB**.




## Sarai Kale Khan RRTS to Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station: At a Glance

| Detail | Current information |
| --- | --- |
| Namo Bharat station | Sarai Kale Khan |
| Railway station | Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station |
| Dedicated connection | Yes |
| Connecting structure | 280-metre Foot Over Bridge |
| Travelators | 6 automatic travelators |
| Escalators | Available on the FOB connection |
| Lifts | Available |
| Road crossing required on the main connection | No |
| Best option with luggage | Dedicated FOB |
| Current access issue | Sarai Kale Khan-side railway entry is undergoing redevelopment |
| Current railway access from Namo Bharat side | Follow signs to Namo Bharat Gate 1/2 and the new FOB |
| Walking time | Typically several minutes; allow extra time for luggage, crowds and finding your platform |

The **280-metre figure refers to the FOB itself**, not the complete door-to-platform journey. Your actual transfer time will be longer because you have to leave the Namo Bharat platform, reach the appropriate concourse/exit, enter the FOB, cross it and then reach the relevant railway entrance and platform. The six travelators reduce the walking effort but do not eliminate the need to walk.




# Why This Interchange Matters

Sarai Kale Khan is being developed as one of Delhi's most important multimodal transport hubs.

At this location, passengers can connect between:

- Namo Bharat
- Delhi Metro
- Indian Railways
- ISBT services
- City buses
- Road transport

NCRTC describes Sarai Kale Khan Namo Bharat station as a major multimodal integration point located close to **Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station, Delhi Metro and Vir Haqiqat Rai ISBT**. It is also strategically important because the three priority Namo Bharat corridors planned in the first phase are intended to converge at Sarai Kale Khan.

For a passenger, however, the most important question is much simpler:

**“I have just arrived at Sarai Kale Khan on Namo Bharat. How do I get to my train at Hazrat Nizamuddin without dragging my suitcase through traffic?”**

The answer is the dedicated FOB.




# The Sarai Kale Khan Namo Bharat to Nizamuddin Skywalk

The connection between the two transport facilities is commonly described as a **skywalk, foot overbridge or FOB**.

The structure is approximately **280 metres long** and was designed specifically to make the transfer between Namo Bharat and Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station easier.

The FOB has:

- **Six automatic travelators**
- Escalators
- Lifts
- A covered pedestrian connection

NCRTC has highlighted the facility as an important accessibility improvement, particularly for people travelling with luggage, elderly passengers, children, women and passengers with reduced mobility.

The FOB became operational for public use in **May 2026**, after the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut [Namo Bharat corridor](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/) itself became fully operational in February 2026.

This distinction matters because some older articles and maps may show the interchange as a planned facility rather than an operational one.




## Step-by-Step: Sarai Kale Khan RRTS to Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station

### Step 1: Get off at Sarai Kale Khan Namo Bharat Station

After your Namo Bharat train arrives at **Sarai Kale Khan**, do not immediately head toward the road or look for an auto-rickshaw.

Instead, remain inside the station environment and look for directional signs for:

**Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station**

The purpose of the multimodal design is to allow you to make the transfer through the pedestrian infrastructure rather than crossing the busy roads outside.

This is particularly useful if you have:

- A large trolley suitcase
- Multiple bags
- Children
- An elderly family member
- A wheelchair
- A tight railway connection




### Step 2: Follow the Signs for the Railway Station

Once you leave the [Namo Bharat](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/) paid area, follow the pedestrian signage pointing toward **Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station**.

Do not assume that the shortest-looking road outside the station is the correct route.

The dedicated FOB exists precisely to remove the need for passengers to negotiate the busy road environment around Sarai Kale Khan.

Before the FOB opened, passengers transferring between the railway station and RRTS frequently had to deal with road traffic and a less convenient pedestrian movement pattern. The new FOB was specifically commissioned to improve this interchange.

### Important

If you see older online instructions telling you to simply walk along the road from the RRTS station to the railway station, treat them cautiously.

The **dedicated FOB is now the key interchange facility**.




### Step 3: Choose Between Stairs, Escalator and Lift

The FOB is equipped with **escalators and lifts**, in addition to the travelators.

This gives you several ways to make the transfer.

### If you have a trolley bag

The **travelator** is generally the most convenient option once you are on the bridge.

### If you are travelling with children

An escalator or lift may be more convenient depending on your luggage.

### If you have heavy luggage

Look for the lift rather than attempting to carry a suitcase up or down stairs.

### If you use a wheelchair

Use the accessible route and ask station staff for assistance if you are unsure which lift or entrance to use.

NCRTC specifically identifies accessibility as one of the benefits of the FOB.




### Step 4: Enter the 280-Metre FOB

Once you enter the bridge, the transfer becomes much simpler.

The FOB is approximately **280 metres long**.

It has **six travelators**, meaning passengers do not have to walk the entire length of the bridge at normal walking speed.

The travelators are particularly valuable when you are:

- Carrying a large suitcase
- Pulling multiple bags
- Travelling after a long train journey
- Travelling with elderly passengers
- Travelling with young children

### How much time does the FOB take?

There is no official fixed “FOB transfer time” published by NCRTC.

A useful planning estimate is:

**About 4–7 minutes for the physical bridge transfer**, depending on whether you use the travelators, how crowded it is and how quickly you move.

With luggage, lifts, queues or platform-finding added, it is sensible to allow **10–15 minutes or more from the Namo Bharat exit to the railway-station access point**.

This is a planning estimate, not an official journey-time guarantee.




### Step 5: Use the Travelators Correctly

The six travelators are one of the most useful features of this interchange.

They are moving walkways rather than trains or escalators, so you can stand on them with your luggage and allow the belt to carry you forward.

### Best practice with luggage

Keep your trolley bag close to you.

Do not leave a suitcase unattended on the travelator.

If you are travelling with several pieces of luggage, keep your group together rather than sending one person ahead to “save time”.

If a travelator is not operating when you arrive, continue along the pedestrian path and use the other available facilities.

**Important:** The presence of six installed travelators does not mean every travelator will necessarily be operating at every moment. Equipment can be stopped temporarily for maintenance, safety or operational reasons.




### Step 6: Reach the Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station Side

At the railway-station end, follow the signs into **Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station**.

This is where the current 2026 construction situation becomes important.

Northern Railway began redevelopment of the **second entry on the Sarai Kale Khan side** of Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station in June 2026.

The redevelopment includes:

- A new staircase
- Escalator
- Lift
- Booking office
- Toilets
- Extension of the deck slab of FOB-2

Because of this work, the existing Sarai Kale Khan-side entry/exit has been temporarily closed. Northern Railway has specifically directed passengers to use **Gate 1 and Gate 2 of the Namo Bharat station via the new FOB** to access Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station.

### This is the most important 2026 update in this guide.

If an older blog tells you to exit directly through the old Sarai Kale Khan-side railway entrance, **do not blindly follow it**.

Follow the current physical signage and railway instructions at the site.




### Step 7: Enter the Railway Station

Once you reach the railway-station side, follow the designated entry route.

You will then need to locate the appropriate railway concourse/platform access for your train.

Remember that reaching **Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station** is not the same as reaching your **train platform**.

Your total journey is:

**Namo Bharat platform**

↓

**Namo Bharat concourse/exit**

↓

**FOB approach**

↓

**280-metre FOB**

↓

**Railway-station entry**

↓

**Security/entry area**

↓

**Railway concourse**

↓

**Your platform**

That is why planning only for the 280-metre distance can produce an unrealistically short connection time.




## Which Hazrat Nizamuddin Gate Should You Use?

This is one of the confusing parts of the interchange because railway-station access arrangements are changing due to redevelopment.

The current Northern Railway instruction is particularly useful:

**Passengers approaching Hazrat Nizamuddin from the Sarai Kale Khan/Namo Bharat side should use Gate 1 and Gate 2 of the Namo Bharat station and the new FOB during the ongoing second-entry redevelopment.**

Therefore, if you arrive by Namo Bharat, your mental route should be:

> **Sarai Kale Khan Namo Bharat → Gate 1/2 direction → FOB → Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station**

rather than trying to locate the old Sarai Kale Khan-side railway entrance first.




## What If I Need a Specific Railway Platform?

This is where you should add extra time.

Hazrat Nizamuddin is a large railway station. The FOB gets you to the railway-station access area, but your train may still be several minutes away on foot.

Before leaving the Namo Bharat station, check:

- Train number
- Train name
- Departure time
- Platform number
- Any platform changes

If your platform has not been announced, use the railway information displays or enquiry facilities once inside the station.

### Don't plan a 10-minute connection

Even though the two transport facilities are physically close, a connection such as:

**Namo Bharat arrival → railway departure in 10 minutes**

is unnecessarily risky if you have luggage.

The safer approach is to build in time for the complete interchange rather than just the bridge.




# Sarai Kale Khan to Nizamuddin: How Long Should You Allow?

There are three different times you should think about.

## 1. Physical bridge time

The FOB itself is approximately **280 metres**.

With normal walking, this is only a few minutes.

Using the travelators can reduce the physical effort considerably.

## 2. Station-to-station transfer time

Include:

- Getting off the train
- Finding the exit
- Walking to the FOB
- Waiting for or using a lift
- Crossing the FOB
- Entering the railway station

A practical planning buffer is around **10–15 minutes**, but busy periods, luggage and temporary diversions can make it longer.

## 3. Train-to-train connection

If you are connecting from Namo Bharat to a long-distance train, add additional time for:

- Railway security
- Finding the correct concourse
- Platform access
- Walking along the platform
- Last-minute platform changes

### Recommended planning buffer

For a comfortable connection, consider reaching Sarai Kale Khan Namo Bharat **at least 20–30 minutes before your railway departure**, and more if you are travelling with several bags or with elderly passengers.

This is a practical recommendation, not an official minimum connection time.




# What About Battery Buggy Services?

This is a question many passengers ask, especially when travelling with elderly people or several large bags.

### Is a battery buggy guaranteed between Sarai Kale Khan RRTS and Hazrat Nizamuddin?

**Do not plan your journey assuming that a battery buggy will definitely be available.**

While the interchange has been designed with accessibility in mind, including lifts and escalators, I could not find a current official NCRTC or Northern Railway source that establishes a regular, guaranteed battery-buggy service specifically for this Namo Bharat-to-railway transfer.

That distinction is important.

A station may provide staff assistance or mobility support on request without having a continuously operating buggy service.

### If you need mobility assistance

Do this instead:

1. Ask Namo Bharat station staff before leaving the paid area.
2. Explain that you are transferring to Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station.
3. Tell them if you are travelling with an elderly, disabled or mobility-limited passenger.
4. Ask which lift/accessibility route you should use.
5. At the railway side, ask railway staff if additional assistance is required.

The FOB itself has **lifts and escalators**, so passengers who cannot comfortably use stairs should not need to rely on the availability of a buggy as their only accessibility option.




# Is There a Travelator on the Sarai Kale Khan Skywalk?

**Yes.**

This is one of the clearest confirmed features of the interchange.

The FOB has **six automatic travelators**. NCRTC has specifically described the 280-metre FOB as a travelator-equipped connection between Sarai Kale Khan Namo Bharat and Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station.

This is particularly relevant to luggage passengers because the travelators reduce the amount of continuous walking required.

### But remember

A travelator is not the same thing as a luggage conveyor.

You still need to:

- Keep control of your suitcase
- Stand safely
- Keep children close
- Follow directional instructions
- Leave the travelator carefully at the end




# What If the Travelator Is Not Working?

Do not turn around or leave the station.

The bridge remains a pedestrian connection.

If a particular travelator is stopped:

1. Continue on foot.
2. Look for the next operating travelator.
3. Use escalators or lifts where appropriate.
4. Ask station staff if you are unsure.

The six travelators provide multiple moving-walkway sections, but equipment availability can vary operationally.




# Is the Skywalk Covered?

The FOB has been designed as a dedicated pedestrian connection, and reporting on the facility has highlighted its pedestrian infrastructure, including travelators, escalators and lifts.

For passengers, the practical advantage is that the transfer is separated from the busy road movement below.

This is particularly useful during:

- Peak traffic
- Rain
- High heat
- Heavy passenger movement
- Large train arrivals

The facility was introduced partly to address the earlier difficulty of passengers crossing or navigating the congested road environment between the two transport facilities.




# What About the Delhi Metro Connection?

Sarai Kale Khan is not only a Namo Bharat and railway interchange.

The area also has the **Sarai Kale Khan-Nizamuddin Metro Station on Delhi Metro's Pink Line**.

This creates another important transfer chain:

**Delhi Metro → Sarai Kale Khan → Namo Bharat → Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station**

or the reverse:

**Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station → Sarai Kale Khan →** [**Delhi Metro**](https://metroguideindia.com/delhi-metro/)

The metro station has three commonly listed access gates, with Gates 2 and 3 serving the Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station side.

NCRTC has also developed a covered pedestrian pathway connecting the Namo Bharat station with the Delhi Metro's Sarai Kale Khan-Nizamuddin station.

**Internal link opportunity:** Link **Sarai Kale Khan-Nizamuddin Metro Station Guide** here.




# The Three-Way Interchange at Sarai Kale Khan

For a passenger, it helps to visualise the area as three connected transport systems.

### 1. Namo Bharat

For regional travel toward:

- [Ghaziabad](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/stations/ghaziabad.html)
- [Murad Nagar](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/stations/murad-nagar.html)
- [Modinagar](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/stations/modi-nagar-south.html)
- [Meerut](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/stations/begumpul.html)

### 2. Indian Railways

Through:

**Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station**

For long-distance and intercity trains.

### 3. Delhi Metro

Through:

**Sarai Kale Khan-Nizamuddin Metro Station**

on the Pink Line.

NCRTC's multimodal planning places these systems in close proximity to each other.

This is why Sarai Kale Khan is increasingly important for passengers making a **rail-to-rail transfer**.




# Namo Bharat to Hazrat Nizamuddin With Heavy Luggage

If you have one backpack, this interchange is relatively straightforward.

If you have two large suitcases, a trolley and a child, your strategy should be different.

## Before leaving Namo Bharat

Make sure:

- Your phone is charged.
- Your train ticket is accessible.
- Your railway platform information is known.
- All bags are together.
- Valuables are with you.

## At the FOB

Use:

**Lift → travelator → lift/escalator**

wherever appropriate.

You do not need to prove that you can walk the entire bridge.

## At the railway station

Once inside, check the platform display again.

Railway platforms can be long, so reaching the station entrance does not mean you have finished the transfer.




# What If You Are Travelling With an Elderly Passenger?

The new FOB is particularly useful in this situation.

Instead of taking an elderly passenger across the road environment outside Sarai Kale Khan, use the dedicated pedestrian connection.

The FOB includes:

- Travelators
- Escalators
- Lifts

NCRTC has specifically identified elderly people, children, women, specially abled passengers and luggage-carrying travellers among those expected to benefit from the facility.

### Best strategy

Do not rush the elderly passenger.

Use the lift where appropriate and allow additional time for:

- Getting off the Namo Bharat train
- Finding the FOB
- Waiting for the lift
- Crossing the bridge
- Entering the railway station
- Reaching the platform




# What If You Are Travelling With a Child?

Keep the child beside you on the travelator.

The moving walkway may be unfamiliar to young children.

When stepping off:

- Hold the child's hand.
- Maintain control of your luggage.
- Do not stop immediately at the end of the travelator.
- Move to the side before reorganising your bags.

The same principle applies when entering an escalator.




# What If You Are Travelling With a Wheelchair?

The interchange has lifts and is designed with accessibility in mind.

However, the best route can depend on which lift is operating and the temporary construction arrangement at the railway end.

Therefore:

**Ask station staff for the accessible route rather than attempting to navigate an unfamiliar construction diversion yourself.**

This is particularly important because the Sarai Kale Khan-side railway entry is undergoing redevelopment.




# Current Construction: What Passengers Need to Know in 2026

This deserves its own section because it is the information most likely to make older online guides inaccurate.

Northern Railway announced in June 2026 that redevelopment work had started at the **second entry of Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station on the Sarai Kale Khan side**.

The planned work includes:

- New staircase
- Escalator
- Lift
- Booking office
- Toilets
- FOB-2 deck extension

The existing Sarai Kale Khan-side entry/exit was closed for the execution of this work. Passengers coming from the Namo Bharat side were instructed to use **Gate 1 and Gate 2 of the Namo Bharat station and the new FOB** instead.

### Why this matters for SEO and real passengers

Many older pages can correctly say that Sarai Kale Khan is connected to Hazrat Nizamuddin but still give the wrong practical access instructions.

A passenger following an old route may walk toward the old railway entry and discover that it is closed.

The safer rule is:

> **Follow current railway/Namo Bharat signage and use the new FOB connection.**




# Sarai Kale Khan RRTS to Hazrat Nizamuddin: Simple Walking Map

Use this mental map:

```plain
SARAI KALE KHAN
NAMO BHARAT STATION
        │
        │
   Namo Bharat
   Gate 1 / Gate 2
        │
        ▼
   FOB APPROACH
        │
        ▼
  280-METRE FOB
        │
   ┌────┴────┐
   │         │
Travelators  │
   │         │

        │

HAZRAT NIZAMUDDIN
RAILWAY STATION
        │
        ▼
Railway entry/concourse
        │

        │
        ▼
     YOUR TRAIN
```

The diagram is deliberately simplified because temporary construction arrangements can change the exact entry path.




# Sarai Kale Khan RRTS to Hazrat Nizamuddin: Estimated Time Breakdown

Here is a more useful way to plan the transfer.

| Stage | Practical planning allowance |
| --- | --- |
| Get off Namo Bharat + find exit | 2–5 min |
| Find FOB approach | 1–3 min |
| 280-metre FOB | 4–7 min |
| Waiting/using lift or escalator | 1–5 min |
| Railway entry | 2–5 min |
| Finding platform | 5–10+ min |
| **Practical total** | **15–30+ min** |

These are **planning estimates**, not published official transfer times.

The actual time can be shorter if you know the station and have light luggage, or longer during crowding, equipment downtime, construction diversions or a long walk to your railway platform.

### For a tight train connection

Use **30 minutes or more as your planning buffer**, particularly if:

- You have heavy luggage.
- You have never used the interchange.
- You are travelling with children.
- You are travelling with elderly passengers.
- Your railway departure is important or difficult to replace.




# Why the 280-Metre Distance Can Be Misleading

Someone searching online might see:

**“Sarai Kale Khan to Hazrat Nizamuddin = 280 metres.”**

That number is not enough to plan your journey.

The 280 metres describes the FOB.

It does **not** account for:

1. Your Namo Bharat train stopping position.
2. Walking from the platform to the concourse.
3. Finding the correct exit.
4. Reaching the FOB.
5. Waiting for an escalator/lift.
6. Crossing the FOB.
7. Entering the railway station.
8. Railway security/entry movement.
9. Finding your platform.
10. Walking to your coach position.

This is why a **15–30 minute transfer window** can be more realistic than a simple “five-minute walk”.




# Is an Auto or Cab Needed?

For the normal Namo Bharat-to-Nizamuddin interchange:

**No.**

The dedicated FOB is specifically designed to connect the two facilities.

Taking an auto or cab can actually introduce another variable because Sarai Kale Khan is a busy transport hub with substantial road traffic.

The FOB gives you a grade-separated pedestrian route.

### When might a road vehicle still make sense?

Consider a cab or assisted road transfer if:

- You have exceptionally large luggage.
- You have mobility needs that cannot be comfortably accommodated through the pedestrian route.
- The FOB is temporarily closed.
- Your destination is not Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station itself.
- Station staff direct you to an alternative route because of operational work.




# What If the FOB Is Closed?

Infrastructure can occasionally be closed for:

- Maintenance
- Safety
- Emergency operations
- Construction
- Security restrictions

If this happens, do not assume an old Google Maps walking route is still the intended passenger route.

Ask:

**“Namo Bharat se Hazrat Nizamuddin railway station ka current pedestrian route kahan hai?”**

Station staff should be able to direct you to the active route.




# A Better Strategy for Connecting Trains

If you have booked:

**Namo Bharat → Hazrat Nizamuddin → Long-distance train**

plan backward from the railway departure time.

For example, if your train leaves at **8:00 PM**, do not plan to arrive at Sarai Kale Khan at 7:45 PM.

Instead, aim to be at the Namo Bharat station early enough to accommodate:

**Namo Bharat arrival → exit → FOB → railway entry → security → platform → coach**

A sensible buffer is particularly important because a missed long-distance train can disrupt the rest of your journey.




# Who Will Benefit Most From the New FOB?

The facility is especially valuable for:

### Outstation passengers

You can transfer between regional rapid transit and long-distance rail without negotiating the road.

### Families

Parents can move children and luggage through a controlled pedestrian connection.

### Senior citizens

Travelators, lifts and escalators reduce the physical burden.

### Passengers with luggage

The moving walkways make the 280-metre connection less tiring.

### Metro passengers

The broader Sarai Kale Khan multimodal hub connects the Namo Bharat station with the Pink Line metro station as well.




# Frequently Asked Questions

##### How far is Sarai Kale Khan RRTS from Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station?

The dedicated FOB connecting the two facilities is approximately **280 metres long**. It includes six automatic travelators, as well as escalators and lifts.

##### Is there a skywalk between Sarai Kale Khan Namo Bharat and Hazrat Nizamuddin?

Yes. A dedicated 280-metre foot overbridge connects Sarai Kale Khan Namo Bharat station with Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station. It opened for public use in May 2026.

##### Does the Sarai Kale Khan skywalk have travelators?

Yes. The FOB has **six automatic travelators**.

##### Are lifts available on the Sarai Kale Khan-Nizamuddin FOB?

Yes. Reporting on the operational FOB confirms the availability of lifts and escalators along with the travelators.

##### Is a battery buggy available from Namo Bharat to Hazrat Nizamuddin?

There is no current authoritative source establishing a guaranteed regular battery-buggy service for this specific transfer. Passengers requiring mobility assistance should ask Namo Bharat or railway staff about assistance at the time of travel.

##### Is the old Sarai Kale Khan-side entry of Hazrat Nizamuddin open?

The Sarai Kale Khan-side second entry is undergoing redevelopment work. Northern Railway announced that the existing entry/exit was temporarily closed and directed passengers to use the Namo Bharat station's Gate 1 and Gate 2 via the new FOB.

##### Which Namo Bharat gate should I use for Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station?

During the current redevelopment arrangement, Northern Railway has directed passengers to use **Gate 1 and Gate 2 of the Namo Bharat station** and then the new FOB to access Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station. Follow the latest on-site signs because construction arrangements can change.

##### How long does it take to walk from Sarai Kale Khan RRTS to Nizamuddin?

The physical FOB is 280 metres. A person walking normally can cover that distance in several minutes, while travelators can reduce the walking effort. For an actual train connection, allow substantially more time because station exits, lifts, the railway entry and platform access are additional parts of the journey.

##### Can I take luggage on the skywalk?

Yes. The FOB is specifically intended to improve interchange for passengers, including those travelling with luggage. NCRTC has highlighted luggage-carrying passengers among the groups expected to benefit from the facility.

##### Can I use the travelator with a trolley bag?

The travelators are intended to facilitate passenger movement across the FOB. Keep your luggage under control and follow any safety instructions displayed at the facility.

##### Is Sarai Kale Khan connected to the Delhi Metro?

Yes. Sarai Kale Khan-Nizamuddin Metro Station is on the Pink Line and forms part of the larger multimodal interchange. NCRTC also describes the Namo Bharat station as being close to the Delhi Metro station.

##### Can I go from Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station to Namo Bharat?

Yes. The same dedicated FOB works in the opposite direction. From the railway side, follow the signs for Sarai Kale Khan/Namo Bharat and use the connected FOB.

##### Do I need to cross the main road between the stations?

The dedicated FOB is designed to provide a grade-separated pedestrian connection, so passengers using the intended interchange route do not need to rely on crossing the busy road between the facilities. The FOB was introduced partly to address the previous road-level pedestrian difficulties.




# The Best Route to Remember

If you remember only one thing from this guide, remember this:

### Namo Bharat → Hazrat Nizamuddin

**Sarai Kale Khan Namo Bharat**

↓

**Gate 1 / Gate 2 direction**

↓

**Follow signs for Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station**

↓

**Dedicated FOB**

↓

**Use travelator / lift / escalator**

↓

**Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station**

↓

**Railway entry**

↓

**Check platform**

↓

**Walk to your coach**

During the current redevelopment of the Sarai Kale Khan-side second railway entry, **do not rely on older instructions pointing you toward the closed/altered entrance**. Use the current signage and the new FOB route.




# Final Takeaway

The **Sarai Kale Khan RRTS to Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station** interchange is now substantially easier than a simple road-level walk.

The key piece of infrastructure is a **280-metre dedicated Foot Over Bridge with six automatic travelators, escalators and lifts**. It was opened to the public in May 2026 and provides a dedicated pedestrian connection between the Namo Bharat station and Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station.

For passengers carrying luggage, the important practical lesson is that **the bridge length is not the same as the total transfer time**. You still need to allow time to leave the Namo Bharat station, find the FOB, use the appropriate vertical-access facility, cross the bridge and reach your railway platform.

The other critical 2026 update is the **redevelopment of the Sarai Kale Khan-side second entry at Hazrat Nizamuddin**. Northern Railway has directed passengers approaching from the Namo Bharat side to use **Namo Bharat Gate 1 and Gate 2 and the new FOB** during the work.

If you have heavy luggage, elderly passengers or children, the most comfortable strategy is therefore:

**Namo Bharat → dedicated FOB → travelator → lift/escalator where required → Hazrat Nizamuddin → platform.**

And if you need mobility assistance, ask station staff rather than depending on an unverified assumption that a battery buggy will be available.

The interchange is designed to make **regional rail + Indian Railways + Delhi Metro** function as one connected transport hub. For passengers, that means the journey is no longer about finding the quickest road between two stations. It is about using the **correct pedestrian connection** and allowing enough time for the complete station-to-platform transfer.
